Boise State Broncos.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide places Spencer Danielson in a programme lineage running from Dirk Koetter through Dan Hawkins, Chris Petersen and Bryan Harsin, and credits him with three consecutive Mountain West titles.
Boise State Broncos.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Boise State Broncos.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Boise State Broncos.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Boise State Broncos.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Boise State Broncos.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide anchors its concern in a single collapse: Boise led the nation with 55 sacks in 2024 and managed 27 last season, allowing 24 points per game.
Boise State Broncos.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide expects the Dylan Riley and Sire Gaines pairing to ease Maddux Madsen's job.
Boise State Broncos.qb_development: Not addressed as a coaching record. The guide records Madsen at 20-6 as a starter with a decline from 62.4% for 3,018 yards and a 23-to-6 ratio to 58.3% for 2,334 yards and an 18-to-9 ratio, recalls he was labelled a game manager when Ashton Jeanty carried the offense, judges him capable of more, and suggests he could be the conference's top quarterback.
Boise State Broncos.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 11 returning starters — totalling 16.
Boise State Broncos.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Boise State Broncos.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Tyler Ethridge arriving from Division II Colorado State-Pueblo.
Boise State Broncos.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect beyond one line addition.
Boise State Broncos.vsin_assessment: Sustained excellence across coaching regimes, with one unit questioned. The guide notes Boise has won big under multiple coaches and credits Danielson with three consecutive Mountain West titles, saying Boise deserves to be Pac-12 favorite with another playoff appearance the bigger realistic goal. It records Danielson's own stated disappointment that the offensive line was not more physical and his expectation that this changes. Its verdict on the defense is that Boise has questions to answer on that side.
Boise State Broncos.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with everything returning, three consecutive conference titles, a senior quarterback the guide says could be the conference's best, two of the league's best offensive linemen, a 1,125-yard rusher backed by an 811-yard partner, and a head coach who has already stated the specific fix he wants up front.
Boise State Broncos.concerns: A sack total that fell from a nation-leading 55 to 27, four of the top five tacklers gone, 24 points per game allowed, and a quarterback whose efficiency declined across the board last season.
Boise State Broncos.betting: The guide expects eight wins if Madsen stays healthy — calling 7.5 a tick low and -135 fair. Its coaching-linked reasoning is the programme's track record of winning under successive coaches.

Colorado State Rams.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and the guide weighs both stops. The Coaching Carousel records that Jim Mora got a second kick at the college coaching can at UConn and did extremely well with it, going 27-23 in Storrs with back-to-back nine-win seasons, and that his first four seasons at UCLA were pretty good before the bottom fell out quickly. The team pages reassess the UCLA tenure — 46-30 from 2012 to 2017 seemed unremarkable at the time, but given the Bruins' subsequent struggles he may have performed better than perceived.
Colorado State Rams.dc: Tyson Summers, retained — the previous regime's coordinator who took over as interim head coach — with Kenny McClendon as co-defensive coordinator, brought from UConn.
Colorado State Rams.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Colorado State Rams.dc_status: Returning — the Coaching Carousel records that to provide some continuity, Mora kept interim head coach Tyson Summers in his previous DC role, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Colorado State Rams.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Colorado State Rams.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records that Mora prefers a running quarterback and that both candidates can run.
Colorado State Rams.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Colorado State Rams.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the preference for a running quarterback.
Colorado State Rams.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records UConn transfer K'saan Farrar possibly having the inside track through his history with Mora despite only 18 career attempts, judges he could struggle to beat Oklahoma State transfer Hauss Hejny, and reports a media source indicating Hejny has become the favorite. Its closing point is a general principle applied here: as with most new coaches, Mora must find a quarterback who can make plays.
Colorado State Rams.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback all change; the defensive coordinator is retained. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 0, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 3.
Colorado State Rams.staff_turnover: Complete except for one deliberate retention. Jay Norvell was fired at midseason, Mora brought several players and coaches from UConn including coordinator Pryce Tracy and co-defensive coordinator Kenny McClendon, and kept Tyson Summers in his previous role.
Colorado State Rams.prior_school: UConn, comprehensively — Mora, coordinator Pryce Tracy, co-coordinator Kenny McClendon, quarterback K'saan Farrar, running back Mel Brown, receiver Jackson Harper, tight end Juice Vereen and linebacker Oumar Diomande, who was second for the Huskies in tackles with 116 and sacks with five. The guide also records Hauss Hejny from Oklahoma State and Durell Robinson from Auburn.
Colorado State Rams.portal_recruiting: The whole rebuild. The guide records Mora integrating more than 60 new players and notes he must build the offensive line through transfers too, a theme it says holds for the whole team.
Colorado State Rams.vsin_assessment: Bet on him rather than against him, with the timeline set out. The Coaching Carousel notes the Rams have not won a bowl game since 2013 and have had a winning record just once since 2017, and suggests Mora's previous stops are examples of what he can do at schools with lowered expectations, much like this one. The team pages reason from precedent — he turned UConn around, going 9-4 and 9-3 in his last two years — call an immediate bowl unrealistic, and supply the UConn trajectory as the model: 6-7 and 3-9 in his first two years before winning big once he had built the roster and found the right quarterback. Their stated position is that after the magic of the past two years it is better to bet on Mora than against him.
Colorado State Rams.strengths: A head coach with back-to-back nine-win seasons at his last stop and a UCLA record the guide says looks better in hindsight, a coordinator and co-coordinator transplanted from that programme with players who already know them, a retained defensive coordinator for continuity, and a defensive front seven the guide says looks strong on paper.
Colorado State Rams.concerns: A Stability Score of 3 with seven returning starters, more than 60 new players to integrate, an unresolved quarterback competition, an offensive line that must be built through transfers, and a defense that ranked 112th in scoring and 125th against the run.
Colorado State Rams.betting: On price the guide notes Circa lists 3.5 including the 12th flex game and recommends Over -140, adding it would not be a big surprise if Mora reached 6-6, especially with impressive quarterback play.
Colorado State Rams.carousel_summary: Adam Burke asks the reader to pause twice — first to come to terms with Colorado State now being in the Pac-12, then to think about Mora, who got a second kick at the college coaching can at UConn and did extremely well with it. He gives the record: the football lifer was 27-23 in Storrs with back-to-back nine-win seasons, which he calls no small feat, and notes his first four seasons at UCLA were pretty good before the bottom fell out quickly. He records the one continuity decision — to provide some continuity, Mora kept interim HC Tyson Summers in his previous DC role — and then the programme's baseline: the Rams haven't won a bowl game since 2013 and have had a winning record just once since 2017. His conclusion is a hypothesis: perhaps Mora's previous stops are examples of what he can do at schools with lowered expectations, much like this one.

Fresno State Bulldogs.previous_hc_experience: Extensive and highly rated. The guide says Matt Entz is about as good as it gets — he coached North Dakota State to two FCS national titles in five years and left 60-11 — and notes he won eight regular-season games in his Fresno debut.
Fresno State Bulldogs.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Fresno State Bulldogs.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Fresno State Bulldogs.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Fresno State Bulldogs.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide states a clear building philosophy: Entz builds winning teams by building a physical offensive line first.
Fresno State Bulldogs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Fresno State Bulldogs.run_pass: Run-first by construction. The guide records Fresno running the ball well last season while being limited by what EJ Warner could not do, and judges Fresno could have the most effective ground offense in a conference rich in running back talent.
Fresno State Bulldogs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide diagnoses last season precisely — an accurate passer without the arm to stretch the field — and is honest that Maryland transfer Khristian Martin's impact is a mystery while noting he has the physical skills for major impact.
Fresno State Bulldogs.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 3 for 13 returning starters, totalling 13.
Fresno State Bulldogs.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Fresno State Bulldogs.prior_school: North Dakota State for Entz. On the roster the guide records Khristian Martin from Maryland.
Fresno State Bulldogs.portal_recruiting: Addressed at quarterback, where Entz brought in Martin to replace EJ Warner.
Fresno State Bulldogs.vsin_assessment: A strong endorsement of the coach with a matchup-level argument attached. The guide says Entz is about as good as it gets, treats the upgraded quarterback position as reason for opponents to beware, and states its conditional precisely: if Khristian Martin matures quickly Fresno can win almost every game, while the team is solid enough everywhere to win seven or eight even with mediocre quarterback play. It explains Entz's method — physical offensive line first — and applies it to a specific game, arguing Fresno's line could push USC around since Lincoln Riley is known for finesse teams that are not the most physical up front.
Fresno State Bulldogs.strengths: A head coach with two FCS national titles and a 60-11 record at his previous stop, both coordinators returning, arguably the biggest and best offensive line in the Pac-12 with three of the league's best linemen, two backs who combined for 1,302 yards, four of the top five pass catchers back, and a physically upgraded quarterback.
Fresno State Bulldogs.concerns: A new quarterback whose impact the guide calls a mystery, and last season's ceiling set by passing limitations the new man has yet to prove he removes.
Fresno State Bulldogs.betting: The guide's conclusion returns to the coach: Entz won eight regular-season games in his debut, has a better team and a manageable schedule, so bet on the Bulldogs being big overachievers. It applies this to two specific games, expecting the USC line to be bet higher by kickoff and flagging a potentially dangerous underdog, recalling Entz coached Fresno to a 30-7 win at Boise as a 17-point underdog last year, and advising bettors to circle both and consider taking the points.

Oregon State Beavers.previous_hc_experience: None as a head coach. The Coaching Carousel records that JaMarcus Shephard is a longtime wide receivers coach, most recently with Kalen DeBoer at both Washington and Alabama, and states plainly that he has never been more than a co-OC or assistant head coach and is now a head coach looking to install a dramatically different offense.
Oregon State Beavers.oc: Mitch Dahlen, part of the Alabama and Washington staffs that developed star quarterbacks.
Oregon State Beavers.dc: Mike MacIntyre, successful at a variety of stops including head coaching jobs at San Jose State, Colorado and Florida International.
Oregon State Beavers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Oregon State Beavers.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Oregon State Beavers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Oregon State Beavers.offensive_scheme: Not named, but the Coaching Carousel records that Shephard is looking to install a dramatically different offense.
Oregon State Beavers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 29.4 points allowed per game and cites evidence of progress in holding Washington State to seven points in a late-season upset.
Oregon State Beavers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Oregon State Beavers.qb_development: Addressed as a staff-quality argument. The guide records Maalik Murphy declining with a bad Oregon State team — 1-7 as starter with 1,805 yards, nine touchdowns and eight interceptions after going 9-3 at Duke — notes his play has not been impressive to watch and that he is not much of a running threat and turns the ball over too much, then concludes that with a better staff and supporting cast, expect significant improvement. It names coordinator Mitch Dahlen as part of the Alabama and Washington staffs that developed star quarterbacks.
Oregon State Beavers.continuity: Broken across the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 6.
Oregon State Beavers.staff_turnover: Complete, after Trent Bray was dismissed following an 0-7 start and the programme finished 2-10. The guide rates the replacement staff a major upgrade.
Oregon State Beavers.prior_school: Alabama and Washington for Shephard and Dahlen, with the guide noting Shephard has Pac-12 history from Kalen DeBoer's Washington staff when the Huskies won the conference. On the roster it records Aeryn Hampton from Alabama, Raesjon Davis as a former USC transfer and Ish Findlayter from Duquesne.
Oregon State Beavers.portal_recruiting: Addressed at specific positions — an Alabama receiver added, and transfers added on defense under MacIntyre.
Oregon State Beavers.vsin_assessment: A directional change credited, with bounded expectations. The Coaching Carousel frames it as going the defensive route not working, so Oregon State has gone the other way, and sets out the context — the Beavers floated around like a feather in the wind when the Pac-12 dissolved, playing as a Pac-12 team in name only and even playing fellow orphan Washington State twice last season, with Trent Bray going 5-14. The team pages judge Jonathan Smith and Oregon State were better off together, expect Shephard to inherit one of the conference's worst teams and possibly the worst, rate the staff a major upgrade with Mike MacIntyre a big part of it, and set expectations deliberately: do not expect Shephard to replicate Smith's win totals, but the Beavers should be more competitive in a rebuilding year.
Oregon State Beavers.strengths: A staff the guide rates a major upgrade, including a coordinator from the Alabama and Washington staffs that developed star quarterbacks and a defensive coordinator with three head-coaching jobs behind him; a returning quarterback with a 9-3 season at Duke on his record; a top returning tackler the guide rates a potential league-best defender; and a front seven it calls solid.
Oregon State Beavers.concerns: A head coach who has never been more than a co-coordinator or assistant head coach installing a dramatically different offense, a Stability Score of 6, a quarterback the guide says turns the ball over too much and is not much of a running threat, and a programme coming off 2-10 with years of instability behind it.
Oregon State Beavers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Oregon State Beavers.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the hire as a reversal of approach: going the defensive route didn't work, so Oregon State has gone in the other direction. He is sympathetic to the predecessor — Tyler Bray really walked into a brutal situation after Jonathan Smith left, as the Beavers floated around like a feather in the wind when the Pac-12 dissolved, playing as a Pac-12 team in name only, mostly facing a Mountain West schedule and even playing fellow orphan Washington State twice last season, before going 5-14. He then introduces Shephard, a longtime wide receivers coach most recently with Kalen DeBoer at both Washington and Alabama, and notes that like Washington State, Oregon State should be ready to invest in the programme with a conference to call home again. His reservation is precise: Shephard has never been more than a co-OC or assistant head coach and is now a head coach looking to install a dramatically different offense.

San Diego State Aztecs.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Sean Lewis promised a quick turnaround on arrival in 2024, went 3-9 with a pile of ugly losses, then delivered 9-4 and a bowl last season.
San Diego State Aztecs.oc: Not addressed in guide. Lewis is described as an innovative offensive coach.
San Diego State Aztecs.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
San Diego State Aztecs.dc_status: New — the guide records Sumler taking over, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
San Diego State Aztecs.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
San Diego State Aztecs.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised: the guide calls Lewis an innovative offensive coach whose remaining problem is finding the right quarterback to run his system, and warns his plans for a high-flying passing attack might not materialise.
San Diego State Aztecs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit ranking No. 6 nationally in scoring defense at 15.4 points per game — company it lists as Ohio State, Indiana, Miami and Texas Tech — pitching two shutouts and allowing more than 24 points only three times.
San Diego State Aztecs.run_pass: Addressed as a dependency: the guide says San Diego State needs an effective ground attack to support a quarterback who needs the help.
San Diego State Aztecs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide sets expectations for Jayden Denegal in both directions — he will never remind San Diego fans of Dan Fouts, but has the potential to be much better than 58.8% completions for 1,807 yards with nine touchdowns and eight interceptions — and reports a troublesome shoulder injury as apparently repaired.
San Diego State Aztecs.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 3 for 13 returning starters, totalling 14.
San Diego State Aztecs.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, and the guide notes the change comes on the unit that drove the turnaround.
San Diego State Aztecs.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Jayden Denegal as a Michigan transfer and Jacob Bostick from Texas A&M.
San Diego State Aztecs.portal_recruiting: Addressed at receiver, with a Texas A&M transfer added.
San Diego State Aztecs.vsin_assessment: A test passed, with an ironic observation and a firm forecast. The guide frames Lewis as a coach who has already answered his first test after a 3-9 debut. Its irony is that the turnaround under an offensive-minded coach was led by the defense, which ranked sixth nationally in scoring defense. It identifies the programme's identity as tough defenses and star running backs, says the running back is unquestionably in place, and sets the ceiling by the defense and quarterback play. Its verdict is blunt: Lewis is a good coach, but it sees a disappointing season and regression as imminent, concluding flatly that this defense will take some steps back.
San Diego State Aztecs.strengths: A head coach the guide calls innovative who delivered a 9-4 turnaround, offensive-coordinator and quarterback continuity, the Mountain West's leading rusher at 1,297 yards, both top receivers returning, and a defense coming off a sixth-place national scoring finish.
San Diego State Aztecs.concerns: A new defensive coordinator inheriting only two returning starters where 10 returned a year ago, the loss of the 27th overall pick from the secondary, an offensive line replacing three starters, and a quarterback the guide says is surrounded by questions.
San Diego State Aztecs.betting: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The reasoning is that optimism is hard to justify with the quarterback surrounded by questions and the defense rebuilding — Lewis is a good coach, but the guide sees a disappointing season and regression as imminent.

Texas State Bobcats.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records G.J. Kinne's first head-coaching stop as Incarnate Word in 2022, where he went 12-2 and was hired away by Texas State, and traces his coaching apprenticeship under Gus Malzahn, Sonny Dykes and Chad Morris.
Texas State Bobcats.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Texas State Bobcats.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Texas State Bobcats.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Texas State Bobcats.offensive_scheme: Not named, but attributed to the head coach: Kinne is described as a former college and NFL quarterback known for creating prolific passing offenses, and the guide records Texas State ranking 12th nationally in scoring offense at 36.5 points per game and fifth in yards at 472 per game.
Texas State Bobcats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records a defense that allowed 164.8 rushing yards per game and 29 points per game with four starters returning.
Texas State Bobcats.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide's emphasis is on Brad Jackson's dual-threat production — 3,224 passing yards with 21 touchdowns plus 744 rushing yards and 17 touchdowns.
Texas State Bobcats.qb_development: Addressed through the head coach's own background. The guide records Kinne as a big-time passer at Tulsa who finished with 9,472 yards and 81 touchdowns, describes him as known for creating prolific passing offenses, and says the numbers will point to Jackson as the marquee Pac-12 quarterback.
Texas State Bobcats.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 13.
Texas State Bobcats.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator per the Stability Score table.
Texas State Bobcats.prior_school: Incarnate Word for Kinne's head-coaching debut; Tulsa for his playing career; and coaching apprenticeships under Gus Malzahn, Sonny Dykes and Chad Morris. On the roster the guide records William Boone from North Carolina and DonTerry Russell as a former Mississippi State transfer.
Texas State Bobcats.portal_recruiting: Addressed at specific positions — a 6-foot-6, 375-pound North Carolina transfer at right tackle, and a former Mississippi State transfer at defensive end.
Texas State Bobcats.vsin_assessment: Consistency credited and the coach identified as a rising commodity. The guide leads with three years producing 8-5, 8-5 and 7-6, each ending in a bowl win, describes Kinne as a former college and NFL quarterback known for creating prolific passing offenses, and projects that in an era when innovative offensive coaches are in high demand he will likely become a hot candidate for bigger jobs, with this season's high-powered offense helping that rise. Its stated risk is the defense, which it calls definitely a concern.
Texas State Bobcats.strengths: Three straight bowl-winning seasons under a head coach the guide expects to attract bigger jobs, a returning quarterback the guide says will be the conference's marquee passer, two of the league's top receivers returning, offensive-coordinator continuity, and a scoring offense ranked 12th nationally.
Texas State Bobcats.concerns: A defense that allowed 164.8 rushing yards and 29 points per game with only four starters returning and a new coordinator, and an inexperienced offensive line.
Texas State Bobcats.betting: The guide draws a direct betting instruction from the coaching profile: look to bet Over the total in most Texas State games this season. It also suggests Jackson could post bigger numbers than Arch Manning both in the opener and over the season.

Utah State Aggies.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and the guide sets it out as a before-and-after. Bronco Mendenhall had 11 years and 99 wins at Brigham Young, then a losing record at every stop since leaving in 2015 — 36-38 in six seasons at Virginia, 5-7 in one year at New Mexico, and 6-7 last year with the Aggies.
Utah State Aggies.oc: Robert Anae, known for aerial attacks.
Utah State Aggies.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Utah State Aggies.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Utah State Aggies.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Utah State Aggies.offensive_scheme: Addressed as a stated tension between coordinator reputation and expected usage: the guide notes Anae is known for aerial attacks but expects more emphasis on the ground game, with senior Javen Jacobs returning as the featured back behind McCae Hillstead.
Utah State Aggies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 28.7 points allowed per game with the worst of it being 55 at Vanderbilt and 44 each at Texas A&M and Hawaii.
Utah State Aggies.run_pass: Expected to shift toward the run despite the coordinator's aerial reputation.
Utah State Aggies.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records McCae Hillstead, a BYU backup a year ago who started four games for Utah State in 2023, winning the job in spring, notes he is also a running threat, and projects the offense's 30.9 points per game will likely decline a little with big shoes to fill.
Utah State Aggies.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9.
Utah State Aggies.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator per the Stability Score table.
Utah State Aggies.prior_school: BYU is the recurring thread — Mendenhall's 99 wins there, Hillstead as a former backup there, and linebacker Harrison Taggart having been at Oregon, BYU and California.
Utah State Aggies.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect.
Utah State Aggies.vsin_assessment: A record held in two halves, and a reputation the guide says has faded. It opens on 11 years and 99 wins at BYU against a losing record at every stop since, and on the defense holds both facts together: Mendenhall was known for producing strong defenses at BYU, but that reputation has faded in recent years. It cites his best win, 28-17 at Fresno State, as a positive sign, and keeps the uncertainty in its verdict — the Aggies will be better defensively, but it is tough to say how much better. It closes with scheduling advice rather than analysis, saying Mendenhall would be wise to arrange a softer nonconference slate in future, contrasting Indiana's Curt Cignetti scheduling cupcakes outside Big Ten play with Utah State lining up Utah and Washington on the road.
Utah State Aggies.strengths: A head coach with 99 wins at BYU and a signature road win at Fresno State, defensive-coordinator continuity, two of the top three tacklers returning including a 114-tackle safety, a veteran interior offensive line, and a quarterback who has started for the programme before.
Utah State Aggies.concerns: A losing record at every stop since 2015, a new offensive coordinator whose reputation does not match the expected approach, replacing a dual-threat quarterback who led the team in rushing, a defense that conceded 55, 44 and 44 in its worst outings, and a road schedule the guide says stacks the odds against a bowl.
Utah State Aggies.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its stated uncertainty at quarterback is the reason for its hedge.

Washington State Cougars.previous_hc_experience: None. The Coaching Carousel records that the 35-year-old Kirby Moore is on the fast track — three years of calling plays at Missouri and one at Fresno State now has him in a head coaching role — and that his time at Boise State crossed over with brother Kellen.
Washington State Cougars.oc: Not addressed in guide. Kirby Moore's own credential is three years as Missouri's offensive coordinator.
Washington State Cougars.dc: Trent Bray, the former Oregon State head coach.
Washington State Cougars.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Washington State Cougars.dc_status: New — the guide records Bray's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Washington State Cougars.play_caller: The guide records Moore designing the plays, with Pinnick, Vorhees and Freeman doing most of the playmaking.
Washington State Cougars.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised by the head coach's record: three years as Missouri's offensive coordinator designing dynamic offenses around dual-threat quarterbacks.
Washington State Cougars.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records Washington State allowing 20.2 points per game to rank 27th nationally last year, blowout losses to North Texas and Washington aside.
Washington State Cougars.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split, though the guide says Pinnick's running ability is what excites the coach.
Washington State Cougars.qb_development: The guide's framing device for the whole programme. It opens on precedent rather than preview: in 2022 an FCS quarterback from Incarnate Word transferred to Washington State, and Cam Ward developed into the real deal over two seasons before becoming the first overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft. It makes the relevance explicit — Washington State is again bringing in an FCS quarterback to revive its offense — and says Caden Pinnick's play will go a long way toward determining how successful Moore is in his first season, adding that Moore outrecruited Colorado for him.
Washington State Cougars.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 1.
Washington State Cougars.staff_turnover: Complete, and the guide's central fact is that this is the third such change in three years: Moore is Washington State's third coach in three years, after Jake Dickert in 2024 and Jimmy Rogers in 2025, with Dickert leaving for Wake Forest and Rogers taking the Iowa State job and several players with him.
Washington State Cougars.prior_school: Missouri, Fresno State and Boise State are Moore's reference points; Oregon State is Trent Bray's. On the roster the guide records Caden Pinnick from UC Davis, Kirby Vorhees from South Dakota State, Tank Hawkins from Florida, Linus Zunk from Vanderbilt, Jalil Tucker from Oregon and Keith Brown as a former Oregon transfer.
Washington State Cougars.portal_recruiting: The rebuilding mechanism, and the guide notes it was forced: Moore had to work the transfer portal to replenish the roster after Rogers left with several players, and found a promising dual-threat quarterback to ease the transition. The Coaching Carousel adds the institutional point — the programme hasn't really been investing in its roster while being a Pac-12 orphan with Mountain West guardianship, and now back in the Pac-12 will invest in the head coach and the roster all at once, which will probably take some time.
Washington State Cougars.vsin_assessment: A promising branch of a good coaching tree, needing time. The Coaching Carousel says grabbing a branch of the Chris Petersen, Kalen DeBoer and Eli Drinkwitz coaching tree is far from a bad idea, but that Moore is going to need to grow into the role at a programme that hasn't really been investing in its roster. The team pages answer their own question directly: a third straight winning season while rebuilding is doubtful, so expect less from Moore's first season. Their closing balance is offense against defense — entertaining potential with Pinnick pulling the trigger, but a defense that appears nowhere near as strong as last year's, which they call a real problem. They separate the hire from the unit: Bray was a good hire, but this defense has a long way to go.
Washington State Cougars.strengths: A head coach with three years designing dynamic offenses around dual-threat quarterbacks at Missouri and a lineage the guide rates highly, a defensive coordinator it calls a good hire, an FCS quarterback the guide compares to a first overall pick's arrival, a returning top receiver and leading rusher, and renewed institutional investment with a conference to call home.
Washington State Cougars.concerns: A Stability Score of 1 with eight returning starters and no returning defensive starters at all, a third head coach in three years, a predecessor who left taking several players, and a defense the guide says has a long way to go after ranking 27th nationally last year.
Washington State Cougars.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its coaching-linked conclusion is that a third straight winning season while rebuilding is doubtful, and that the Cougars could get into many high-scoring games.
Washington State Cougars.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames Moore as a coach on the fast track: his time at Boise State crossed over with brother Kellen, who has a slightly more high-profile job, and while the 35-year-old isn't coaching the Saints like his 37-year-old brother, three years of calling plays at Missouri and one at Fresno State now has him in a head coaching role. He rates the pedigree — grabbing a branch of the Chris Petersen, Kalen DeBoer, Eli Drinkwitz coaching tree is far from a bad idea — then states the constraint: he's going to need to grow into the role with a programme that hasn't really been investing in its roster while being a Pac-12 orphan with Mountain West guardianship. His conclusion is about timing: now back in the Pac-12, the programme will invest in the head coach and the roster all at once, and that will probably take some time.
